subject.title: feat(agents): configured agent env reaches spawned subprocesses

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad literal `agents.list[].env` across CLI, exec, ACP/ACPX, and stdio MCP child processes, or wait for the narrower exec-only SecretRef direction from PR #96309?
rationale: Both approaches solve agent-scoped subprocess env, but they create different public config, secret-handling, and upgrade contracts that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Approve broad agent env
options.body: Accept this PR's all-child-process literal `agents.list[].env` contract and require green exact-head CI before merge.

options.title: Prefer exec-only SecretRef
options.body: Pause this PR and move the canonical design to the narrower `agents.list[].tools.exec.env` SecretRef path in PR #96309.

options.title: Split the surface
options.body: Keep the cross-runtime plumbing work only after revising the public config shape and docs to match the maintainer-approved boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve broad agent env
recommendation.body: Accept this PR's all-child-process literal `agents.list[].env` contract and require green exact-head CI before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the prior maintainer review requirements for the predecessor per-agent env PR and are the clearest owner for deciding whether this implementation satisfies that contract.
